title: On‑Prem / VPC Reproducible Benchmark Harness for Customer Environments
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: Build a reproducible, low-friction benchmark harness that customers and Redwood SRE can run inside Private/VPC/on-prem clusters to measure tokens/sec and p95 tail latency for real-serving workloads, and to enable regression detection against a recorded baseline. This ticket delivers: (1) a containerized harness image and run script that does not require outbound telemetry, (2) a canonical YAML config schema for reproducible runs (model, sequence lengths, concurrency, batching, KV cache warmup steps), (3) a compressed artifact format with metadata for later regression analysis, and (4) a minimal offline analyzer that compares runs to baseline and raises alerts when p95 or tokens/sec regress beyond thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Harness image (gcr.io/redwood/perf-harness:eng-8273) can be deployed in a VPC-only cluster with no outbound network access and produce an artifacts tgz containing raw traces and a run_manifest.json
Canonical config supports: model name, quantization profile, sequence length distribution, request concurrency, batching window, KV cache warmup iterations, and a seed for synthetic prompt generator

Automated analyzer produces a report with tokens_per_sec, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, median_latency_ms and highlights regressions where p95 increased by >10% or tokens/sec decreased by >8% compared to baseline
End-to-end reproducibility: running the same manifest on the same infra image reproduces tokens/sec within ±5% and p95 within ±8% across 3 runs
Documentation and runbook published to Confluence and linked in attachments, and SRE/solutions engineering have validated the flow in two distinct customer-like VPC clusters
testing_plan: Step 1: Pull benchmark image and run local smoke with --dry-run flag to validate config parsing
Step 2: Deploy harness as a Kubernetes Job in a private cluster (no egress) with config set A (8xA100 equivalent), collect artifacts to PVC, compress to tgz
Step 3: Run analyzer locally against baseline artifact s3://redwood-perf/baselines/8xA100-default.tgz to create regression report
Step 4: Repeat runs with 4xA100 and CPU-only variants to validate cross-variant comparisons
Step 5: Execute reproducibility test matrix (3 runs per config) and record variance metrics to dashboard
runbook_snippet: # Collect artifacts: kubectl cp perf-harness:/workspace/artifacts ./artifacts && tar czf eng-8273-$(date +%F).tgz ./artifacts
implementation_notes: Privacy constraint: harness cannot rely on external telemetry endpoints. Use local collectors that write to PVC and support syslog or upload via customer-approved tools (scp/s3/gcs via preseeded creds).

Performance measurement: measure tokens/sec at the token-emitter boundary (post-decoding) to avoid network serialization noise; include synthetic prompt generator with real-world distribution sampling.
Warmup strategy: mandate KV cache warmup iterations configurable by percent of dataset; default 5k tokens of warmup or 30 seconds, whichever comes first.
Regression thresholds: conservative defaults (p95 +10%, tokens/sec -8%) but make thresholds configurable per-customer; allow historical windows (7/14/30 days) for trend detection.

Trade-offs considered: full-fidelity traces vs. smaller artifact size. Chosen approach: collect aggregated latency histograms + sampled raw traces (1 per 1000 requests) to balance forensic value with upload costs.
